items.question_md: Demonstrate how a eukaryotic cell is organized with the support of a labelled diagram and state the key roles of mitochondria, lysosomes, Golgi bodies, vacuoles, and endoplasmic reticulum.
items.answer_md:
**Organisation of a eukaryotic cell.** A eukaryotic cell has a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles, each a compartment with its own job (division of labour).

**Labelled diagram (described):** an outer *plasma membrane* (phospholipid bilayer) enclosing *cytoplasm*; centrally a *nucleus* (nuclear envelope with pores, chromatin, nucleolus); in the cytoplasm the *rough ER* (ribosomes on its surface) continuous with the nuclear envelope, *smooth ER*, *Golgi apparatus* (stack of flattened cisternae, cis face towards ER, trans face outwards), *mitochondria* (double membrane, inner folds = cristae, matrix), *lysosomes* (small vesicles), *vacuoles*, free *ribosomes* and the *cytoskeleton*. (A plant cell adds cell wall, chloroplasts and a large central vacuole.)

**Key roles**

| Organelle | Structure | Key role |
|---|---|---|
| Mitochondria | double membrane, cristae, own DNA and 70S ribosomes | Site of aerobic respiration (Krebs cycle, electron transport chain); makes ATP, the "powerhouse" |
| Lysosomes | single-membrane vesicles with hydrolytic enzymes (acidic pH) | Intracellular digestion of food, worn-out organelles (autophagy) and bacteria; "suicide bags" |
| Golgi bodies | stack of cisternae | Modify, sort, package and secrete proteins and lipids (glycosylation, vesicles); forms lysosomes |
| Vacuoles | membrane-bound sacs (tonoplast); large in plants | Store water, salts, wastes, pigments; maintain turgor pressure; in animals food and contractile vacuoles |
| Endoplasmic reticulum | network of membranous tubes and sacs | **RER**: protein synthesis and transport; **SER**: lipid/steroid synthesis, detoxification, Ca$^{2+}$ storage |

items.question_md: Differentiate between the following terms (mention two differences): Karyokinesis and Cytokinesis
items.answer_md:
| Karyokinesis | Cytokinesis |
|---|---|
| Division of the nucleus | Division of the cytoplasm |
| Occurs first (prophase to telophase) | Occurs after (or along with) telophase, completing the cell division |

items.question_md: Differentiate between the following terms (mention two differences): Animal and Plant Cells
items.answer_md:
| Animal cell | Plant cell |
|---|---|
| No cell wall, only plasma membrane | Cellulose cell wall outside plasma membrane |
| No chloroplasts; small or no vacuoles; centrioles present | Chloroplasts present; large central vacuole; centrioles usually absent |

items.question_md: Differentiate between the following terms (mention two differences): Germ Cells and Somatic Cells
items.answer_md:
| Germ cells | Somatic cells |
|---|---|
| Form gametes (sperm, egg); haploid ($n$) after meiosis | Form body tissues; diploid ($2n$) |
| Divide by meiosis; pass genes to the next generation | Divide by mitosis; not passed to offspring |

items.question_md: Differentiate between the following terms (mention two differences): Anaphase and Telophase
items.answer_md:
| Anaphase | Telophase |
|---|---|
| Centromere splits; sister chromatids pulled to opposite poles | Chromatids have reached poles; chromosomes decondense |
| Nuclear envelope absent | Nuclear envelope and nucleolus re-form around each set; spindle disappears |

items.question_md: Differentiate between the following terms (mention two differences): Gene and Genome
items.answer_md:
| Gene | Genome |
|---|---|
| A segment of DNA coding for one protein or RNA | The complete set of DNA (all genes plus non-coding DNA) of an organism |
| One of many units on a chromosome | Total genetic content of a haploid set; e.g. human genome about 3 billion base pairs |

items.question_md: With reference to the human digestive or skeletal system, present a labelled diagram and explain how its design and function reflect engineering principles. Hint: (Process engineering: mechanical and chemical conversion of raw materials into usable energy, with by-product management. Structural and mechanical engineering: load distribution, strength, flexibility, and motion.)
items.answer_md:
**Digestive system as a process plant** (skeletal system could equally be chosen).

**Labelled diagram (described):** mouth (teeth, tongue, salivary glands) -> pharynx -> oesophagus -> stomach -> small intestine (duodenum, jejunum, ileum) with liver, gall bladder and pancreas attached -> large intestine (caecum, colon) -> rectum -> anus.

**Engineering mapping**

| Stage | Biological action | Process-engineering principle |
|---|---|---|
| Mouth | Teeth crush food; salivary amylase starts starch digestion | Size reduction (crusher) raises surface area; first reactor with enzyme catalyst |
| Oesophagus | Peristalsis pushes the bolus | Conveyor with pumping action, works against gravity |
| Stomach | Churning plus HCl (pH 1.5-2) and pepsin | Stirred acidic batch reactor; acid kills microbes, activates pepsin; mucus lining = corrosion protection |
| Small intestine | Bile emulsifies fats, pancreatic enzymes and intestinal enzymes finish digestion; villi and microvilli absorb | Neutralising stage (bicarbonate) then separation unit; villi give huge surface area for mass transfer, counter-current-like blood flow |
| Large intestine | Water and salt reabsorbed; bacteria ferment residue | Dewatering and by-product recovery (vitamin K, water) |
| Rectum / anus | Faeces stored and egested | Waste storage and valve-controlled discharge (sphincters) |

**Structural and mechanical points:** layered muscular wall (circular and longitudinal muscle) gives flexible tubing that withstands pressure and moves contents by peristalsis; sphincters (cardiac, pyloric, ileocaecal, anal) act as one-way control valves; the liver is the processing and by-product unit (bile, detoxification, storage).

**Result:** raw food is mechanically and chemically converted to absorbable nutrients (glucose, amino acids, fatty acids) that fuel ATP production, with wastes managed in a continuous, controlled flow line.

items.question_md: Describe the major human organ systems and explain how they have influenced innovations in engineering design.
items.answer_md:
**Major organ systems and the engineering they inspired**

| System | Function (brief) | Engineering innovation |
|---|---|---|
| Digestive | Breaks down food, absorbs nutrients | Chemical reactors and bioreactors, peristaltic pumps, heat/mass exchangers with large surface area |
| Respiratory | Gas exchange in alveoli, ventilation by diaphragm | Ventilators, oxygenators (heart-lung machine), gas-exchange membranes |
| Circulatory (cardiovascular) | Heart pumps blood through closed vessels | Pumps, pacemakers, artificial heart and valves, fluid-network and pipe-flow design, stents |
| Excretory | Kidneys filter blood, regulate water and salts | Dialysis machines, membrane filtration, process control |
| Skeletal and muscular | Support, levers, movement, protection | Truss and beam design, load-bearing structures, prosthetic limbs, joint implants, robotics and exoskeletons |
| Nervous | Sensing and signal transmission through neurons | Sensors, feedback control, artificial neural networks, brain-computer interfaces, bionic ears (cochlear implants) |
| Endocrine / immune | Chemical regulation; defence | Chemical control systems, biosensors, anomaly-detection and security systems |

Theme: biomimetics. Nature gives optimised feedback control (homeostasis), efficient flow networks, light strong structures (bone) and self-repair, and engineers copy these in devices and design.

items.question_md: A bacterial strain has invaded the human respiratory system. Initially, 100 cells enter the body. Each bacterial cell divides every 20 minutes (doubling time = 20 min). The immune system becomes active after 1 hour of infection and can kill 70% of the existing bacterial population every 20 minutes once activated. Estimate the total number of bacterial cells remaining after 3 hours of infection.
items.answer_md:
**Given:** $N_0=100$, doubling time 20 min, immune system active after 1 hour, kills 70% of the population every 20 min thereafter. Total time 3 h = 9 intervals of 20 min.

**First hour (3 intervals, no immunity):**
$N_{60}=100\times 2^{3}=800$ cells.

**Next 2 h (6 intervals):** in each interval the population doubles and then 70% die, so it is multiplied by $2\times0.3=0.6$.
$N_{180}=800\times(0.6)^{6}=800\times0.046656\approx 37.3$

**Result: about 37 bacterial cells remain after 3 hours** (the infection is being cleared).

items.question_md: A cell divides every 30 minutes. Determine the total cell population after 7 hours if a culture system initially contains $2 \times 10^{3}$ cells.
items.answer_md:
**Given:** $N_0=2\times10^{3}$, generation time $g=30$ min, $t=7$ h $=420$ min.

**Formula:** $N=N_0\,2^{n}$, with $n=t/g$.

$n=420/30=14$ generations.

$N=2\times10^{3}\times2^{14}=2000\times16384=32{,}768{,}000$

**Result: $N\approx3.28\times10^{7}$ cells.**
